title: ZenaTech Details ZenaWorx Drone-Based Construction Intelligence Platform Targeting AI Data Center Development
summary: ZenaTech Details ZenaWorx Drone-Based Construction Intelligence Platform Targeting AI Data Center Development Drone-captured LiDAR, 3D progress monitoring and digital terrain […]
body_markdown:
***Drone-captured LiDAR, 3D progress monitoring and digital terrain modeling are designed to support construction visibility and recurring service relationships from earthworks through structural development***


**Vancouver, British Columbia, (October 20, 2026)** — ZenaTech, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) (“ZenaTech” or the “Company”), a technology solution provider specializing in AI (Artificial Intelligence) drone, Drone as a Service (DaaS), enterprise SaaS, and Quantum Computing solutions, today outlined the capabilities and commercial strategy behind ZenaWorx, its drone-based construction monitoring software targeting AI data centers, infrastructure and public works projects. The[ZenaWorx construction monitoring software](https://www.zenatech.com/zenatech-expands-zenaworx-drone-based-construction-monitoring-software-to-include-digital-terrain-modeling-and-signs-first-ai-data-center-customer/) combines aerial data collection with software-based site modeling and analysis to help construction teams understand conditions on the ground, track changes over time and compare construction progress against project plans. The platform is being developed through collaboration between ZenaTech’s enterprise SaaS and Drone as a Service (DaaS) divisions.


“AI infrastructure is built in the physical world, and every phase of that build depends on accurate, repeatable measurement,” said Shaun Passley, Ph.D., CEO of ZenaTech. “With ZenaWorx, we are combining our Drone as a Service field locations network with drone data and software to give customers a consistent view of their projects from earthworks through structural development. That turns what has traditionally been a one-time survey visit into an ongoing relationship that can span the full life of a multi-year project, and we believe it could be a meaningful recurring revenue opportunity as we focus on adding customers and scaling this service across our network.”


ZenaWorx is designed to function as[construction progress monitoring software](https://www.zenatech.com/zenatech-enters-the-ai-data-center-construction-market-with-zenaworx-a-drone-based-3d-digital-progress-monitoring-software/) , turning drone-captured LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) data into three-dimensional representations of construction sites. By collecting data at successive stages of construction, the platform is intended to help project teams identify differences between measured conditions and planned designs.


Its planned capabilities and applications support the work of surveyors, engineers and construction managers by providing additional measured site information such as:


- **3D construction progress monitoring:** Creating digital site models that help teams review structural and site development over time
- **Digital terrain modeling:** Representing ground elevations and surface conditions to support earthworks planning and monitoring
- **Cut-and-fill measurement:** Measuring the volumes of material removed or added during site preparation
- **Grading assessment:** Comparing measured elevations and slopes with engineering plans
- **Drainage assessment support:** Providing terrain information that helps qualified project professionals evaluate drainage conditions
- **Repeat site comparisons:** Using successive surveys to document changes and support standardized progress reporting


AI data center campuses can involve substantial land preparation, grading, drainage and phased construction, and ZenaWorx is being designed to give project teams visibility into each stage through repeat aerial data collection and software-based reporting. During initial earthworks, terrain models can support assessment of site elevations and material movement. As construction advances, updated 3D models are intended to help teams track physical progress and compare measured conditions against project plans. Underpinning this approach is a continuing record of site development, with customers able to access updated information at agreed intervals throughout a project.


ZenaWorx is being offered through ZenaTech’s[Drone as a Service](https://www.droneasaservice.com/) network, allowing customers to access[drone construction monitoring](https://www.droneasaservice.com/construction-progress-update/) services without purchasing and operating their own drone fleets. The service is designed to be subscription-based for repeat-service arrangements spanning the life of construction projects, and the platform’s terrain modeling and progress-monitoring capabilities are also intended to address commercial construction, and public works needs, including landfill earthworks and municipal infrastructure projects.


ZenaWorx was introduced in May 2026, and in August 2026 the Company announced its first paying customer for[AI data center construction monitoring](https://www.zenatech.com/zenatech-expands-zenaworx-drone-based-construction-monitoring-software-to-include-digital-terrain-modeling-and-signs-first-ai-data-center-customer/) and the addition of beta-stage digital terrain modeling. Additional updates will be provided as ZenaWorx service and product advancements and customer milestones are achieved.


**About ZenaTech**[ZenaTech](https://www.zenatech.com/) , Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) is a technology company that specializes in AI autonomy drone platforms to transform commercial, government, and defense sectors. Its subsidiaries include drone manufacturing through ZenaDrone, a global[Drone as a Service](https://www.droneasaservice.com/) (DaaS) business, and an enterprise SaaS division of software brands. The Company is executing an acquisition-led DaaS roll-up strategy to digitize and automate legacy service industries like land surveys and inspections, driving drone-based scalable, recurring revenue growth. With an operating footprint spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia, ZenaTech is advancing AI drones for applications such as agriculture and logistics, as well as ISR, cargo, and counter-UAS for U.S. defense and NATO allies. The company is investing in next-generation technologies, including drone swarms, quantum computing, and advanced AI autonomy to capture long-term opportunities in key markets through its R&D initiatives.


**About ZenaDrone** ZenaDrone, a subsidiary of ZenaTech, develops and manufactures AI-powered multifunction autonomous drone solutions integrating machine learning, predictive analytics, and advanced computing technologies, for government, defense, and industrial applications. This includes multifunctional drones for surveying, inspections, logistics, security, and defense applications. Its product portfolio under development includes the[ZenaDrone 1000](https://www.zenatech.com/drone-technology-solutions/) for ISR defense and specialized cargo, the[IQ Nano](https://www.zenatech.com/drone-technology-solutions/) for indoor inventory management and security, the[IQ Square](https://www.zenadrone.com/zenadrone-iq-square/) for outdoor inspections and maintenance, the[IQ Quad](https://www.zenadrone.com/iq-quad-drone/) for land surveying, the IQ Aqua, for underwater applications, and the IQ Octo for precision agriculture. ZenaDrone operates three global manufacturing facilities in Arizona, Dubai, and Taiwan, and is advancing counter-UAS maritime interceptor drones and an integrated defense system.
